entities.name: Spinal NMEP sensory origin
observations: In seven surgical patients, collision testing indicated that high-cervical spinally elicited peripheral-nerve responses labeled NMEPs primarily followed sensory SEP pathways rather than a propagated motor volley.
The spinally generated descending volley collided with the ascending sensory volley from tibial-nerve stimulation, while the peripheral motor volley did not show the same behavior.

entities.name: Antidromic sensory response
observations: Peripheral-nerve responses after spinal stimulation are antidromic for sensory afferents, traveling from the spinal site toward the dorsal-root ganglion and peripheral nerve.
In cats, dorsal rhizotomy abolished the ipsilateral peroneal-nerve response, identifying recruitment of afferent fibers.

entities.name: Spinal stimulation mixed recruitment
observations: Spinal stimulation is not exclusively sensory under all conditions: low-intensity stimulation produced dorsal-root/peroneal-nerve sensory responses, whereas higher intensity produced ventral-root and muscle motor responses.
Motor responses persisted after dorsal rhizotomy, indicating recruitment of nonsensory motor pathways; interpretation depends on intensity, electrode location, and recording site.

entities.name: Antidromic sensory fiber classes
observations: Intraspinal stimulation elicited short-latency antidromic A-fiber responses and, at higher intensity, long-latency antidromic C-fiber population responses in the sural nerve.
Conduction velocities, collision tests, and dorsal-horn dependence supported sensory antidromic recruitment.
